edges.rationale: IBM Security Verify supports the creation, storage, and management of digital representations of cybersecurity roles and their associated permissions and responsibilities. It also supports the assignment of roles to user identities. To be able to create, store, and manage these representations of user roles and responsibilities, the roles and responsibilities themselves must have already been established.

IBM Security Verify supports issuance, storage, management, and revocation of identities and their associated roles and credentials. It also supports the verification of credentials when performing user and device authentication.

IBM Security Verify supports the ability to determine whether an access request is authorized. It authenticates the user or device that is requesting access by verifying the credentials that are bound to the user or device and asserted as part of the access request. The user and device identities must be asserted for this component to be able to authenticate them.

The core function of the RadiantOne Identity Data Manager (IDDM) is to abstract identity and credential data from multiple disparate sources of truth and build an aggregated 360-degree view of the user record. IDDM can span multiple HR platforms, directories, cloud platforms, IGA and PAM solutions, applications, risk engines, and flat files to create as rich and complete a user profile as possible. This Master User Record is then modeled into PE- and application-specific views tailored to the schema, structure, format, and protocol that each consumer of this identity data needs. The concept of “building it once, using it everywhere” not only greatly reduces integration costs and time, but also ensures that all security decisions across all PEs and applications are being made based on the same vetted data from sources of truth. The IDDM platform is capable of reflecting changes in near real-time from enabled systems, and scaling to hundreds of millions of users while maintaining necessary performance. IDDM supports the inclusion of additional objects from contractors, partners, vendors, coalition partners, and non-person entities (NPEs).
